explanation: This pole is a retrospective detector for text that is written in a fixed documentary format rather than free prose: it peaks on the token that fills a conventional slot of that format - a licence or copyright restriction clause ('without the express written permission of the publisher', 'the specific language governing permissions and limitations'), a patent preamble ('the [present] invention relates generally/broadly to'), a biographical parenthetical ('(born 28 July 1992)', '(b. 1992)'), a bibliographic citation line ('et al.'), a legal case caption ('..., a Corporation Not For Profit'), a URL path ('/post/2010/09/'), or a code import/annotation/HTML class name. It is the slot and not the token - 'permissions' to 'rights', 'generally' to 'broadly' and 'born' to 'b' all keep the peak where it is, while the identical clause in a plain sentence, in ordinary legal prose, or behind a narrative lead-in stays at or below 0.35, well under the 0.48 active threshold on the 1.91 scale; known leftovers are the rare political adverb 'legislatively', which fires on its own (judicially/statutorily/ministerially do not), and the code-notation family, which only reaches threshold inside a real code block.
